profile.headline: Undergraduate Research Student
profile.summary:
I am a recent graduate from Oregon State University where I majored in Computer Science with a focus in Artificial Intelligence and a minor in Mathematics. I was born and raised here in Oregon, and I have come to love so much that this state has to offer. One of my biggest hobbies is hiking and this summer I took a road trip through a few national parks for the first time, allowing me to see a different side of this country that I hadn’t seen before. 

In the summer of 2021, I worked as a virtual instructor teaching kids elements of machine learning, advanced python, and cryptography. In late 2020, I started doing some undergraduate research focused on networks and security. Currently, I am developing programs in micropython and collecting data for a radio frequency fingerprinting lab. In my final year in college, I joined my school's Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition (CCDC) team where we won our regional competition and placed 5th at nationals.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Student
positions.description:
Under the guidance of a professor, I researched and analyzed the coexistence capabilities of WiFi and 5G devices in the 6GHz band. Using the Ns3 simulator package, I developed a program to simulate the coexistence of these devices in an indoor scenario.

I researched and presented on wifi security protocols including WEP, WPA, WPA2, and WPA3. For each, I detailed their weaknesses, improvements from the previous specification, and potential vectors of attack. 

Most recently, I am developing programs in MicroPython to enable IoT (Pycom) devices to communicate with each other and establish a TCP connection. Using these programs I am collecting transmission signals for all 50 Pycom devices which will be used to train a machine-learning algorithm to enable device fingerprinting.
positions.insights: Skills: Mathematics · Research · Statistics · Computer Networking · MicroPython

positions.title: Senior Capstone - Collision Avoidance for Autonomous Mobile Robots
positions.description:
Over the course of 9 months, three other students and I worked in a group partnered with PreAct Technologies to enable collision avoidance for autonomous mobile robots. The first few months were focused on breaking down the project to outline its requirements, goals, stakeholders, success measures, timeline, and sprint breakdown. The remaining months were spent developing software for our project and creating a video presentation and display for the College of Engineering Expo.

This project was done using the agile framework with two weekly meetings with our project partner and with our class teaching assistant. The project breakdown was done in Jira with the project split into sprints and each sprint broken down into individual tasks that were assigned to each member. Jira was also used to monitor progress of the project and team member contribution.

The final deliverables were a demonstration video, a presentation at the engineering expo, and the software developed to enable collision and cliff avoidance for simulated data. (The code for the project can be found below in the projects section)
positions.insights: Skills: Communication · Python (Programming Language) · Agile Project Management · Computer Vision · Jira

positions.title: Virtual Tech Camp Teacher
positions.description: Taught kids ages 12-18 concepts of machine learning, cryptography, and advanced python. Developed additional material for students who were more advanced and for others who were interested in other machine learning concepts. Met with other instructors bi-monthly to discuss methods to improve class and engagement. Organized and facilitated final meetings with parents so students could share their accomplishments.

projects.title: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting Dataset
projects.description: This project is a part of the RF fingerprinting lab I am currently working under. For this lab, I developed programs for devices acting as the station node (STA) and the access point (AP). The STAs connect to the APs which tell them when to start transmitting. Once the STA's get the message to start transmitting, they send random messages via UDP packets which we collect and use to create our dataset. The dataset is used to train machine learning algorithms to identify the devices based on how they transmit signals. So far, this dataset is comprised of an indoor and outdoor scenario. Each scenario is made up of 5 days of collection where 5 transmissions from each of the 50 devices are collected for each day.

projects.title: Collision Avoidance for Autonomous Mobile Robots
projects.description: This was the senior project that I worked on at OSU. The goal of this project was to create programs that, using a time of flight camera, could detect objects and drop-offs in a scene and use these to demonstrate collision and cliff avoidance. I was responsible for creating programs to convert scene images to their 3D representation (point clouds), to detect objects in the scene, and develop rules to determine if the objects or drop-offs are in the robot's path.

organizations.name: Security Club: Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition Team
organizations.description:
This club was organized by Oregon State University's Security Club where we competed at the regional and the national competition. The basis of the competition is for each team of students to protect their computers and the services running on them from cyber threats. The scoring is based on the time the team is able to keep their computers and services up, the number of times a device is compromised, and the team's ability to respond to regular business activity simulated by the organizers. 

As a part of this team, we met weekly to discussed best practices for defending linux and windows machines. Specifically, I focused on different configurations for the firewall to control and monitor the flow of information between our internal network and the outside world. Our team won the regional competition and placed fifth at the national competition.
